title: Self-clearing fusible capacitor plate burns out pinhole leakers at sort
idea: 1955 lens (metallized-paper capacitors self-heal by vaporizing the electrode around a fault): insert a 2-3 nm fusible Al/Zn interlayer between the high-k and the TiN top plate. At wafer sort a 1.8x Vcap clearing pulse makes each defect's own leakage current oxidize or evaporate a ~30 nm disc of interlayer around the pinhole. That cuts the defect off while the cell keeps >97% of its Cs.
why: Removes the dielectric-leakage share of the retention tail without remapping cells. High-k can be ~10% thinner (more fF) because rare pinholes no longer set its minimum thickness. ~1.3-2x tail retention on dielectric-limited cells.

title: Electrometer driven-guard midpoint gives the inner access transistor zero Vds
idea: 1955 lens (electrometers kill leakage by driving the guard to the signal's own potential): split the access path into two series transistors. A tiny source follower, gated by the storage node, drives the midpoint, so in hold the inner device has Vds~0 and its subthreshold/GIDL current collapses. The follower's only load is the outer transistor's off-leakage, so standby current stays at pA.
why: Subthreshold current scales with (1-exp(-Vds/kT)). Nulling Vds to <10 mV cuts the access-leakage component 10-50x, so refresh can be 4-10x rarer for access-limited cells. The two extra devices sit in a stacked tier over the capacitor.

title: Symmetric bipolar chopper access device: no gate oxide, no GIDL
idea: 1955 lens (symmetric alloy-junction transistors served as bilateral choppers): replace the MOSFET with a vertical n+/p/n+ pillar whose two n+ ends (bitline side and storage side) are identical, with the wordline contacting the p-base directly. Base at -0.5 V isolates the bit behind two reverse-biased junctions. Base at +0.8 V conducts both ways, since inverse beta equals forward beta.
why: No gate oxide means no GIDL, no oxide-trap VRT and no short-channel subthreshold path. Off-leakage becomes pure junction generation, for ~2-4x retention, and there is no thin gate dielectric left to scale.

title: Paraelectric storage dielectric makes plate-pulse boost state-dependent at read
idea: 1958 lens (varactor parametric amplifiers got gain from a pumped nonlinear capacitor): use a strongly tunable paraelectric (Ba,Sr)TiO3-type storage dielectric, biased so a '1' node sits at low field (high eps) and a '0' node at high field (low eps). A plate pulse just before wordline-on couples a larger fraction of its swing into '1' nodes than into '0' nodes, because coupling is set by eps contrast against the node parasitic. That adds a few hundred mV of separation, so a half-decayed '1' still reads clean.
why: Turns ~3:1 eps tunability into ~2x effective read signal. Retention can then be defined at a much deeper decay point: ~2x longer refresh interval and ~40-50% lower refresh energy, with the access device unchanged.

title: Photomultiplier-style avalanche stage multiplies cell charge before sensing
idea: 1955 lens (photomultiplier dynodes turn a few electrons into a measurable pulse): put a linear-mode impact-ionization stage at each local-bitline input to the sense latch. It is a short gated n+/p-/p+ junction biased just below breakdown, which multiplies the few-fC packet dumped by the cell ~10x (excess-noise factor ~2) before latching.
why: Retention is limited by sense margin, not by total charge. A 10x charge gain lets cells decay to ~1/5 of today's fail point, for ~3-5x longer refresh interval and proportionally fewer refresh bitline swings.

title: Grid-leak bleeder drains floating-body holes from vertical access pillars
idea: 1955 lens (a tube's grid-leak resistor bleeds charge that would otherwise self-bias the grid): give each vertical-channel access pillar a deliberately resistive (~1e12 ohm) body strap, a thin lightly doped p- neck to a shared hole-sink line. GIDL- and impact-generated holes then drain in microseconds instead of piling up and lowering Vt during hold.
why: Floating-body charging is a top retention killer for 4F2 vertical-channel DRAM. A high-ohmic bleed keeps Vt stable without loading fast access, recovering ~5-10x retention compared with fully floating pillars.

title: Traveling-wave-tube helix: spiral gate lengthens access channel without area
idea: 1955 lens (TWT helices slow a wave by forcing it along a spiral): etch the vertical access pillar with a helical gate trench, so the channel winds ~2.5 turns around the pillar. That gives ~80 nm of effective gate length inside a 12 nm x 12 nm footprint, while a thin helical body keeps drive acceptable.
why: Effective L rises 3-4x at constant area. DIBL falls from ~100 to <20 mV/V and short-channel off-current drops ~10x at equal Vt. That can buy ~4x longer refresh or a lower wordline voltage.

title: Vertical-blanking refresh: hide refresh inside AI training communication phases
idea: 1955 lens (TV hid beam retrace inside a scheduled blanking interval): during all-reduce/collective phases, when HBM traffic dips, the accelerator runtime broadcasts a 'blanking' hint. The HBM controller banks postponed refreshes, using a widened postpone/pull-in window, and fires them all-bank inside those predictable windows.
why: Refresh steals 10-20% of bandwidth at 32-64 Gb densities. Aligning it to idle phases recovers most of that (~+10-15% usable HBM throughput) without changing refresh count or cells.

title: Refresh sweep as free tabulator: hash every refreshed row for dedup
idea: 1955 lens (IBM tabulators extracted statistics while cards streamed past anyway): refresh already senses every row once per 32-64 ms. A narrow hash unit at each bank edge taps the row buffer at low duty, computes a 64-bit signature of the row being refreshed and streams it to the host, which merges identical and zero pages copy-on-write.
why: Turns mandatory refresh energy into a free full-memory content scan. Dedup and zero-page merging typically free 10-30% of capacity in VM/cloud fleets, doing DRAM's job with less DRAM.

title: Read-after-write verify catches half-charged cells masquerading as leakers
idea: 1955 lens (tape drives verified every block with a read-after-write head): after a write burst, the bank senses the written columns against a raised reference (~70% VDD). It rewrites, with a stretched tWR, only columns that never reached full level: high storage-contact-resistance cells that otherwise start each retention period half charged.
why: At advanced nodes many 'weak retention' cells are really weak-write cells. Verifying writes strips them from the tail, allowing ~1.5-2x longer refresh intervals for a few % of write bandwidth.

title: Tetrode screen electrode shields storage junctions from passing wordlines
idea: 1955 lens (the tetrode's screen grid shields the control grid from the plate): line the buried-wordline trench wall facing the neighbor's storage junction with a thin grounded conductive screen (doped poly or TiN tied to p-well potential). Passing-gate swings and negative hold bias then stop modulating that junction's surface field.
why: Passing-gate-induced leakage is a dominant tail term in buried-wordline 6F2 arrays. Screening it can tighten the retention tail ~2x and decouple each cell's retention from neighbor activity.

title: Destructive quantum-interference molecular junction as near-zero-leak access switch
idea: 2100 lens (molecular electronics matured): the access element is a monolayer of meta-linked, cross-conjugated aromatic molecules between storage and bitline electrodes. Their off-state transmission sits on a destructive-interference antiresonance, 1e4-1e6 below a para-linked analog. A gate electrode shifts the molecular levels ~0.5 eV off the antiresonance to switch on.
why: Isolation set by wave interference rather than a thermionic tail sidesteps the 60 mV/dec Boltzmann limit in principle. Target is <0.01 fA off-current in a molecule-scale footprint.

title: Phononic delta-layer superlattice starves trap-assisted generation of phonons
idea: 2100 lens (designer phonon spectra): build the storage-junction depletion region as silicon with sub-monolayer Ge delta-sheets every ~2 nm. These open phonon minigaps that remove the optical-phonon modes deep traps need for multiphonon emission, while barely touching the electronic gap.
why: Thermal generation via a midgap trap needs ~10-20 phonons emitted. Starving the needed modes could cut SRH generation and phonon-assisted tunneling several-fold (speculative 3-10x) at the same defect density.

title: Redox-molecule storage node holds charge behind a reorganization-energy barrier
idea: 2100 lens (molecular charge storage replaces bare capacitors): graft a monolayer of redox-active molecules (porphyrin/ferrocene class) onto the storage electrode, so stored charge sits in discrete oxidation states. Discharge needs electron transfer over a ~0.5-1 eV Marcus reorganization barrier, while a write simply drives the electrode past the redox potential.
why: Charge locked behind a chemical barrier can retain for seconds to minutes instead of 64 ms, potentially cutting refresh ~100x and adding charge density. Ns-speed redox and endurance are the open risks.

title: Oxygen-reservoir plate electrochemically refills dielectric vacancies during idle
idea: 2100 lens (self-healing materials): use an oxygen-buffering top electrode (IrO2/RuO2 on ZrO2). In scheduled idle slots, a brief reverse-polarity plate bias pumps O2- ions from the reservoir back into field-grown oxygen-vacancy chains in the high-k, electrochemically un-forming incipient leakage paths at room temperature (ionic drift, not heat).
why: Capacitor dielectric leakage creeps up with stress as vacancies migrate. Periodic electro-ionic healing pins it near time-zero, enabling thinner, higher-Cs dielectrics and ~2x better end-of-life tail retention.

title: Charge-state preset pulse locks bistable defects out of leaky VRT states
idea: 2100 lens (defect-by-defect engineering): VRT cells come from metastable defects that flip between low- and high-generation configurations depending on their charge state. A short substrate preset pulse in each refresh burst floods the junction with carriers, so these defects capture charge and relax into the low-leakage configuration, where a ~0.5 eV configurational barrier holds them until the next pulse.
why: VRT forces a 2x+ refresh guardband because profiling cannot catch future flips. Pinning defects in their benign state removes that guardband, for ~1.5-2x longer refresh.

title: Graphene-silicon barristor: gate tunes Schottky barrier height to isolate bit
idea: 2100 lens (atomically thin contacts tuned like gates): the access device is a vertical graphene/n-Si Schottky junction whose barrier height a gate shifts through graphene's low density of states. Off, the storage node faces a ~0.9 eV barrier with no channel to leak through. On, the barrier is pulled low enough for thermionic write current.
why: A ~0.9 eV thermionic barrier implies ~1e-20 A leakage for a 10 nm contact, in a 4F2 vertical footprint. Barrier-height physics replaces short-channel physics, but the needed ~0.7 eV tuning range is beyond today's graphene.

title: Local stress detunes midgap traps away from midgap in storage depletion
idea: 2100 lens: SRH generation scales as 1/cosh((Et-Ei)/kT), so moving a midgap trap only 0.1 eV off center cuts its generation ~50x. Build a permanent 1-2 GPa uniaxial stress field (stressed liner/epitaxial stressor) concentrated in the storage-junction depletion region. Orient it so the deformation potentials of the dominant midgap defects shift them off midgap relative to Ei.
why: Attacks generation per defect rather than defect count, a lever that stacks with purity. Potentially 3-10x lower junction-leakage tail.

title: Ferroelectric domain-wall conduction as a write-and-erase access channel
idea: 2100 lens: in insulating LiNbO3/BiFeO3 films, charged domain walls conduct while the bulk is a >3.5 eV insulator. The access device is a nanoscale ferroelectric valve: a gate pulse nucleates a conducting head-to-head wall linking bitline and storage contacts for the access, then a reverse pulse erases it, leaving channel-free insulating bulk in hold.
why: Hold isolation comes from a wide-gap insulator with no channel at all, targeting sub-aA leakage. The switching physics is ferroelectric, independent of silicon subthreshold behavior.

title: Thermally gated barrier: nano-heater opens a tall wall only during access
idea: 2100 lens: isolate the bit with a ~0.9-1.0 eV heterobarrier that carriers essentially never cross at 300 K. Open it with a ~2 ns Joule pulse through a nano-heater wordline that lifts the barrier region to ~900 K, raising thermionic transmission by ~1e9-1e10 for the access window.
why: Isolation becomes a pure Boltzmann-factor barrier (~1e-20 A at room temperature) with no field-effect tail, decoupling hold leakage from gate control. Heat crosstalk and access energy are the risks.

title: Gated thyristor self-latching cell replaces refresh with pA holding current
idea: 1970s-without-DRAM lens (four-layer Shockley-diode memories were the era's latch): each bit is a vertical p+/n/p/n+ pillar thyristor with a wordline gate on the p-base. A '1' latches on and is held by regeneration at ~10 pA, using deliberately low-beta, recombination-engineered bases; a '0' stays off and blocking.
why: No storage capacitor and no refresh. Holding current of ~5 mA per Gb (half the bits '1') rivals self-refresh current but frees all refresh bandwidth, in a 4F2-compatible pillar.

title: Pfann zone-refined crucible-free 300 mm substrates from US polysilicon rods
idea: 1955 lens (Pfann's 1952 Bell Labs zone refining): grow array substrates by float-zone or cold-crucible induction-skull pulling, using FZ-grade polysilicon rods from US poly plants (MI/TN/WA) and pulled in US crystal plants. FZ is scaled to 300 mm with magnetically stabilized melt zones, so oxygen is <1e16 cm-3 and metals <1e9 cm-3, with no quartz crucible anywhere.
why: Removes the oxygen-precipitate and crucible-metal generation centers that populate the junction-leakage tail (~2-3x tail retention). Also eliminates the HPQ crucible chokepoint with an all-US chain.

title: US-enriched 28Si epitaxial layer cools array hot spots, slowing leakage
idea: 2100 lens (isotope engineering is routine): enrich silicon to >99.9% 28Si in US gas-centrifuge cascades (Piketon-type American centrifuge plants plus ORNL's stable-isotope program) running SiF4. Deposit it as a ~20 um epitaxial layer under the array, where the higher thermal conductivity spreads heat away from hot spots under stacked logic.
why: Junction leakage roughly doubles every ~10 C. Shaving 3-5 C off HBM/DRAM hot spots buys ~1.3-1.4x retention with no circuit change, using only grams of US-enriched material per lot.

title: Atom-counted monolayer doping fixes dopant count per access channel
idea: 2100 lens (atomically precise manufacturing): replace channel implants with a self-assembled monolayer of dopant-bearing cage molecules (carborane-class boron) whose packing lattice fixes areal dopant density. After capping and a spike drive-in, each 12 nm channel gets a dopant count with sub-Poisson variance. Uses only US-made ALD/anneal tools and US-synthesized precursors.
why: Random-dopant fluctuation drives much of the Vt tail behind the ~13 fA worst cell. Halving sigma-Vt lets the tail cells hold ~3-5x longer, or lets mean Vt drop for lower wordline voltage.

title: Selenium valence-mended silicon surfaces around storage junctions and STI
idea: 1955 lens (selenium rectifiers showed Se bonds cleanly to semiconductor surfaces): before liner deposition, terminate the STI sidewalls and storage-contact silicon with a self-limiting Se monolayer (H2Se or Se vapor) that satisfies every dangling bond, then seal it with ALD nitride. The Se comes from US copper-refinery anode slimes (UT/TX).
why: STI-edge and contact surface states are prime generation sites. A covalently complete chalcogen termination can cut surface generation velocity ~10x and, unlike H, cannot be stripped by hot carriers, for ~1.5-2x tail retention.

title: Plasma-free thermal atomic-layer etch near storage junctions on US tools
idea: 1955 lens (every 1950s etch was wet and damage-free): replace the plasma etches closest to the storage junction (storage-contact open, buried-wordline recess) with US-developed thermal ALE. Fluorination plus ligand-exchange cycles run on US-built tools, so no ion bombardment or plasma UV ever reaches the junction.
why: Plasma charging and VUV damage seed interface traps and generation centers exactly where tail cells leak. Damage-free etch trims the tail ~1.5-2x and needs no EUV.

title: Epitaxial crystalline-oxide interface under buried-wordline gate dielectric
idea: 2100 lens (perfect interfaces): grow the first gate-dielectric monolayers on the recess sidewall as a lattice-matched crystalline oxide (SrO/SrTiO3 or Gd2O3, building on ORNL/Motorola US epitaxy) with US-built MBE/ALD tools, then complete the stack with amorphous high-k. The resulting Si-oxide interface is atomically ordered, with Dit ~1e9 instead of ~1e11 cm-2 eV-1.
why: Interface traps drive trap-assisted GIDL, subthreshold-slope loss and RTN/VRT. ~100x lower Dit sharpens slope and cuts trap-assisted leakage, for ~2x tail retention.

title: Magnetron microwave anneal heals implant damage without spreading junctions
idea: 1955 lens (radar magnetrons): activate storage-junction implants with US-built variable-frequency microwave annealing at ~450-550 C wafer temperature. Microwaves couple preferentially into amorphized and damaged silicon and dopant-vacancy complexes, dissolving the end-of-range loops that low-budget spike anneals leave in the depletion region.
why: End-of-range defects inside the depletion region are a classic source of high-leakage tail cells. Selective low-temperature healing keeps junctions shallow and graded, for ~1.5-2x tail improvement.

title: Bridge expansion joint decouples capacitor-stack stress from storage junctions
idea: 1955 lens (bridges survive because expansion joints stop stress transmission): insert a thin compliant layer, either low-modulus porous oxide or a deliberate sliding nitride/oxide interface, between the 1.5-2 um capacitor stack/support lattice and the active silicon. Stack and BEOL stress then stop reaching storage junctions. All films come from standard US-made CVD tools.
why: Stress-induced dislocations and strain-enhanced generation near junctions worsen as capacitors grow taller. Cutting junction stress ~5x removes a tail component that degrades every node, for ~1.3-2x tail retention.

title: Leakage-ratioed loadless static cell built on US mature nodes
idea: 1970s-without-DRAM lens (designers would have squeezed static cells instead): a 4-transistor loadless cell whose PMOS access devices are deliberately sized for ~10x more off-leakage than the NMOS pull-downs across corners. The leakage from precharged bitlines then holds the '1' node itself, with no refresh and no load devices. Built in US 22-65 nm fabs, no EUV.
why: Zero refresh energy and no refresh bandwidth loss, ~2x denser than 6T SRAM. It can absorb the hottest, most-refreshed working set from DRAM using purely domestic mature capacity.

title: Permeable-base vertical access: buried Schottky grating pinches channel off
idea: 1970s lens (MIT Lincoln Lab's permeable-base transistor): make the access device a vertical silicon pillar with an embedded molybdenum-silicide grating, from US-mined Mo, acting as a Schottky gate driven by the wordline. Its depletion pinches the grating openings shut at zero-to-negative bias, with no gate oxide and no inversion channel.
why: Depletion pinch-off isolation removes oxide-related GIDL and Dit leakage paths (~2-3x lower tail leakage) in a 4F2-compatible vertical geometry, with a tungsten-free, all-US materials set.

title: Anti-kick trace cancels wordline turn-off charge injection into cells
idea: 1970s lens (sample-and-hold designers cancelled switch charge injection with matched dummies): each wordline driver also drives a complementary anti-kick trace routed beside the storage contacts with matched overlap capacitance. It swings opposite the wordline at turn-off, so the net coupled charge on the storage node is near zero. Fabricated in US fabs reusing existing layers.
why: Turn-off kickback costs ~50-100 mV of a ~400 mV sense margin. Restoring it gives ~1.3-1.5x longer retention and fewer refresh cycles.

title: Energy-service shared-savings contracts finance low-refresh US memory retrofits
idea: 1970s lens (energy-crisis ESCOs paid for retrofits out of metered savings): a US memory maker installs low-refresh, US-fabbed modules in hyperscale and federal data centers at no upfront cost. For five years it is paid a share of the metered DRAM idle-power savings, measured by module power telemetry.
why: Refresh energy is invisible in $/GB pricing. Shared-savings contracts monetize 30-50% idle-memory power cuts and fund domestic low-leakage capacity.

title: Surface-acoustic-wave conveyor ferries charge into cells without a gate channel
idea: 1970s lens (US SAW-filter and acoustic-charge-transport heritage): coat each subarray with a piezoelectric AlN film sputtered from US-made targets. A GHz SAW burst from an interdigital transducer creates moving potential wells that carry charge over a fixed ~0.8 eV electrostatic barrier between bitline and the row selected by a phase-matched gate. With no SAW running, the barrier is static and channel-free.
why: Gating moves from a field-effect channel to an acoustic potential that is simply absent in hold: no subthreshold channel and no GIDL. One transducer serves a whole subarray, which also trims periphery.

title: Heavy-hole PMOS access cells revive 1970s PMOS to cut tunneling leakage
idea: 1970s lens (PMOS was the first MOS memory technology): flip array polarity to a p+ storage node in an n-well with a PMOS buried-wordline access device. GIDL and gate leakage must then be carried by holes, whose heavier tunneling mass and ~4.5 eV SiO2 barrier (vs 3.1 eV for electrons) suppress band-to-band and oxide tunneling. Uses existing modules in US DRAM/logic fabs.
why: GIDL and oxide tunneling are major tail terms in high-field buried-wordline cells, and PMOS shows several-fold lower GIDL. That gives ~2x tail retention, trading ~2x lower drive for the time budget refresh frees.

title: CAFE-style fleet standard for memory idle energy per gigabyte-hour
idea: 1970s lens (1975 EPCA fleet fuel-economy standards): DOE sets a sales-weighted fleet-average standard for DRAM self-refresh/idle energy (mW per GB at 45 C) with tradable credits. Federal procurement gets bonus credits only for modules fabricated and assembled in the US.
why: Creates market pull for refresh-reduction tech that $/GB competition ignores, steering US fabs to low-leakage cells. A 2x fleet idle-energy gain frees ~15-30% of server memory power.

title: NIST leakage-tail reference wafers and open retention test chip
idea: 1955 lens (the National Bureau of Standards made each new technology measurable first): NIST issues a Standard Reference Material wafer with calibrated fA-level leakage and VRT-emulator structures. It pairs this with an open retention test chip run at SkyWater and US university fabs, so any US team can measure a new access device's ppm tail at 85 C in weeks.
why: Shared, trusted fA metrology cuts the capital needed to qualify new access-device physics ~100x, speeding domestic adoption of refresh-reducing devices.

title: Bell-1952-style open symposium licensing a low-leakage access module
idea: 1955 lens (Bell Labs' 1952 symposium licensed the transistor to all comers for $25,000): a federally funded lab develops a complete low-leakage access-transistor module (recipe, PDK, reliability data). It licenses the module to every US fab for a flat fee after a week-long hands-on symposium, with a US-manufacture clause.
why: Turns a know-how-gated module into a commodity across US fabs (memory, analog, foundry), multiplying domestic DRAM-class capacity paths and spreading refresh-reducing tech fast.

title: Halide-free molybdenum buried wordline from US ore removes fluorine traps
idea: 1955 lens (tube makers chose molybdenum grids for clean, stable surfaces): replace the WF6-CVD tungsten buried wordline with molybdenum deposited by halide-free metal-organic ALD from US-mined Mo (CO/ID). This stops fluorine diffusing into the gate dielectric and forming border traps at the storage-side overlap.
why: Fewer fluorine-induced border traps cut trap-assisted GIDL and RTN-driven VRT (~1.5x tail). It also removes the tungsten chokepoint (China ~80%) and lowers thin-line wordline resistance.

title: Multibeam direct-write storage contacts eliminate overlay-driven GIDL tail
idea: 1970s lens (IBM's EL-1 e-beam systems wrote custom chips directly in the 1970s): write the storage-contact and wordline-recess layers with US-made multi-column e-beam direct write, aligned die by die. This removes the scanner-to-scanner overlay error that shifts the gate-storage overlap and creates high-GIDL tail cells.
why: A few nm of overlay error modulates gate-drain overlap, and GIDL responds exponentially. Halving overlay sigma tightens the GIDL tail ~2x and takes foreign scanners off two critical layers.

title: Muller C-element self-timed refresh sequencer with no clock tree
idea: 1955 lens (David Muller's speed-independent circuits at Illinois): in self-refresh, replace the oscillator, counters and clock distribution with a ring of Muller C-elements that passes a refresh token subarray to subarray. Each step completes only when that subarray's sense amps report done. Built in US logic processes.
why: At low temperature the controller, oscillator and clock tree are a large share of IDD6. Clockless handshaking removes ~20-40% of self-refresh power and naturally staggers current peaks.

title: Western Electric 1956 control rules on inline interface-trap metrology
idea: 1955 lens (the 1956 Western Electric Statistical Quality Control Handbook): after each buried-wordline oxidation and storage-contact clean, measure Dit and surface generation lifetime contact-free on every wafer with US-built corona-Kelvin/photoconductance metrology. Western Electric run rules then flag drift, and the next lot's anneal time and ambient adjust automatically.
why: The leakage tail is set by process excursions, not the mean. Catching Dit drift within a lot cuts tail-outlier wafers ~2x, so refresh specs can be set on a tighter distribution.
